subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — OmniHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@omnihealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — OmniHealth

Hi Ana (and team),

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

Key pain points you called out:
- Slow customer-facing search & summarization pipelines (latency spikes during peak hours)
- Rising inference costs as you scale to multi-model ensembles for personalization
- Need for strict data controls / regional residency for PHI-adjacent logs

Primary goals for the bake-off:
1) Confirm whether Redwood can deliver sub-150ms median token latency for live-search traffic at 80 RPS
2) Demonstrate a 25-40% unit-cost reduction vs your current serving setup using batching + KV caching
3) Validate that private deployment options meet your residency and KMS requirements

Decision criteria (what matters most):
- Latency SLOs (p95 & p99),
- Cost per 1k tokens at scale,
- Deployment model & security evidence (SOC2, KMS integration),
- Support for canary rollouts & A/B testing for model variants

Open questions we captured:
- Which model family will you prioritize for the POC (LLM vs smaller reranker + LLM combo)?
- Do you need a dedicated GPU allocation or is shared dedicated enough for the test window?

Proposed next steps:
- We’ll circulate a short bake-off test plan with concrete workloads (latency + throughput tests) — target delivery: tomorrow EOD PT
- Technical sync with Rishi to align on infra and data paths — can you share two 60-min slots next week?
- Provide SOC2 and data-residency docs (we have a SOC2 report and a private deployment checklist)

Attachments: we will send a test plan and our SOC2 pointer in the next email.

If that summary looks right, we’ll kick off the test plan and schedule the tech sync.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — OmniHealth

Thanks Marissa — this captures things well. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Model family: for the initial bake-off we want to evaluate both a smaller reranker + LLM fusion (our preferred path) and a single LLM baseline. We'll share sample prompts and reranker configs by EOD Monday.
2) Residency: we require logs and debug traces to be stored in our US region only during the POC; access controls need to be scoped to our security group.

Availability for the tech sync next week:
- Tue 20 Apr 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 21 Apr 14:00-15:00 PT. Please lock one if that works.

Also looping in Procurement — please treat this as an exploratory POC; we'll share an internal SOW request if the bake-off looks promising.

—Ana

Thanks Ana — Tue 20 Apr 10:00 PT works for the tech sync; I’ll send the calendar invite.

Quick technical note + proposed bake-off plan (high level):
- Workloads: (a) 80 RPS steady-state with 512 token avg; (b) spike test to 250 RPS for 2 mins; (c) 1k-concurrent small-reranker throughput test.
- Metrics to capture: median latency, p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate.
- Data handling: for POC we’ll mount a read-only sample dataset (anonymized) and capture debug logs to an S3 bucket in US-East with restricted IAM; logs will be purged at POC end unless you instruct otherwise.

I attached a more detailed test plan (spreadsheet) with step-by-step tests and expected pass/fail thresholds. Please review and let us know any changes.

Attachment: redwood-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx

On Tue I’ll also walk through the private deployment options and KMS integrations. If Procurement wants, we can share the SOC2 report after the tech sync.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — received the plan and we’ll review with infra tomorrow. A couple of open items before the sync:

- SOC2: we need either the report or at minimum the SOC2 type II date and auditor name so our InfoSec can do a quick triage.
- Data residency: confirm that debug logs and KV cache snapshots can be restricted to our US bucket — we need a short write-up on that flow for our security review.
- Who will run the burst test — Redwood or our infra team? We prefer Redwood to drive it so we can measure the service-as-a-black-box latency.

Procurement — can you confirm whether a one-off POC SOW is required before the tests start? If so, we can share a draft.

—Ana
